facts.title: thermal release during routine operation on P-7111

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 1 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control BUND_AND_DRAINAGE_CONTAINMENT: the secondary containment by bund and drainage had degraded below its design intent, and the root cause analysis classified this as a task or environmental condition.
Control EMERGENCY_ISOLATION_ON_RELEASE: the emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment was not in place, and the root cause analysis classified this as an absent or failed defence.
Control SEAL_FACE_TEMPERATURE_ALARM: the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip was never verified as effective, and the root cause analysis classified this as an absent or failed defence.
Control SEAL_SUPPORT_SYSTEM_INTEGRITY: the integrity of the mechanical seal support system was never verified as effective, and the root cause analysis classified this as an absent or failed defence.

recommendations: Restore the emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment on P-7111 and record the field verification before this task is next authorised.
Restore the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip on P-7111 and record the field verification before this task is next authorised.
Restore the integrity of the mechanical seal support system on P-7111 and record the field verification before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in responding to a loss of containment, specifically isolating and depressuring a leaking system. P-7111 (export transfer pumps) is in service for tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family. The task proceeded during routine operation while the secondary containment by bund and drainage had degraded below its design intent. The thermal energy involved is held as hot surface, and the recorded presentation was burn, ignition, scald.
response.summary: On 9 March 2015 an incident occurred on P-7111 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during routine operation, releasing thermal energy held as hot surface.
